# tmvp

> tmvp is one CLI that lets an agent read — and, when the user asks, change — every system of one product (postgres, mysql, mongo, redis, nats, kafka, k8s, ssh, scripts, web apps, HTTP APIs (OpenAPI), gRPC, prometheus, loki, grafana, elasticsearch/opensearch, git, gh, aws, gcp, az) across all its environments at once. Reads batch across envs; writes go one target at a time via `tmvp write … --reason`; secrets are `$(commands)` and never leave the local server's memory.

Learn from the CLI itself: `tmvp envs`, `tmvp systems`, `tmvp <env> <system> ls`, `tmvp verbs [type]`, `tmvp llms [topic]`, and `--llmhelp` on any command. Every topic below prints with `tmvp llms <topic>`; `tmvp llms --full` prints everything.

## Docs

- [overview](docs/llms/overview.md): mental model, discovery commands, grammar, output
- [install](docs/llms/install.md): install the binary, external CLIs, first skill
- [config](docs/llms/config.md): config.yaml — vars, secrets, $(…), $file(…), ${file:…}, ${X:-d}, labels, via, login, limits, assets paths
- [writes](docs/llms/writes.md): read vs write vs destructive, --reason, --preview, guards, audit
- [code-mode](docs/llms/code-mode.md): `tmvp code run` — one program for multi-step investigations, saved scripts, writes, safety
- [cost-and-timeouts](docs/llms/cost-and-timeouts.md): read cost guard — estimate before run, too_expensive, --timeout precedence, --force, per-type estimators
- [errors](docs/llms/errors.md): error codes and exit codes, what to do for each
- [server](docs/llms/server.md): the auto-started local server, env vars, lifecycle
- [skills](docs/llms/skills.md): building a skill on tmvp — layout, saved items, good and bad practice
- [environment-variables](docs/llms/environment-variables.md): secrets from .env files ($dotenv) and env vars; TMVP_* settings
- [secret-managers](docs/llms/secret-managers.md): sec, LastPass, 1Password, Bitwarden, Vault, AWS/GCP/Azure, Doppler — install + config line
- [why-fast](docs/llms/why-fast.md): skill shape with a daemon behind it — vs plain skills and MCP servers
- [examples](docs/llms/examples.md): three agent incidents across environments, with and without tmvp (times, password leaks)
- [troubleshooting](docs/llms/troubleshooting.md): symptom → fix
- [environments](docs/llms/environments.md): which env runs — positional/-e > TMVP_ENV > `tmvp use` > default_env > all; batch; --force on protected writes
- [secrets](docs/llms/secrets.md): `tmvp secrets status|audit`, `tmvp certs` — secret health, value-changed, cert expiry (never values)
- [logs-and-metrics](docs/llms/logs-and-metrics.md): where are my logs/metrics (OpenTelemetry lands in loki/prometheus/elasticsearch/grafana/cloud logs) → which tmvp type + verb
- [doctor](docs/llms/doctor.md): `tmvp doctor` — installed tools, server, supported types, per-system secrets/login/connectivity, top fixes

<!-- docs/llms/overview.md -->

# tmvp overview

Teams want one way to diagnose an issue across their products and environments. tmvp formalises that process: your coding agent (Claude, Codex, …) or an engineer looks into logs, runs database queries and inspects queues across dev, staging and prod — under a policy that keeps the systems up and the credentials untouched, from one simple configuration.

- **Nothing goes down.** Reads run read-only (read-only transactions, method allowlists), with row caps and timeouts; a query estimated to run too long — the 2-hour scan that would stall production — is refused before it starts.
- **No silent writes.** A read can never write. A write is only `tmvp write <env> <system> … --reason "…"`, one target, `--preview` first, `--force` on protected envs — and every write is in the audit log (`tmvp logs --writes`), so "who ran that UPDATE?" always has an answer.
- **Credentials untouched.** Config holds references (`$dotenv(.env.prod, KEY)`, `${VAR}`, `$(secret-manager cmd)`); tmvp's local server resolves them. The agent sees names, never values.
- **Batch across environments.** `tmvp all db query "…" --diff` runs once on every env and returns only what differs.
- **Fast.** A background server keeps connection pools, ssh tunnels and fetched secrets alive between calls, and runs envs in parallel; an agent calling `psql`/`ssh` directly reconnects and re-authenticates every time (local demo: one call across 4 envs ≈ 17 ms vs ≈ 500 ms for four separate `psql` runs; the gap grows behind jump hosts).

**Start simple, grow per repo.** tmvp works with just a config file (`~/.tmvp/<product>/config.yaml` or `--config`). When you want more, create a skill in each repo (`tmvp new skill <project>`, or let `/tmvp-discoverer` build it): config plus references and saved queries, so every agent working in that repo knows your environments and how to diagnose them.

A product is described by a **skill**: a folder with `SKILL.md`, `config.yaml` (envs → named systems; secrets only as references) and `assets/` (saved queries, scripts, pages, apis).

## Mental model
- **Product** — one `config.yaml`. A skill can never reach another product.
- **Env** — `dev`, `staging`, `prod`, … Each env has `destructive: true|false`.
- **System** — a named thing in an env (`db`, `cluster`, `admin`) with a `type`
  (postgres, k8s, web, …), fields, optional `labels` and `via` (tunnel chain).
- **Verb** — what you can do to a system type (`query`, `get`, `logs`, `ls`, …). Every verb is
  `read`, `write`, `destructive` or `read-write`.
- **Reads** batch across envs in parallel. **Writes** go one env/system at a time through
  `tmvp write … --reason`.

## Discover everything from the CLI (start here)
```
tmvp envs                         # envs, destructive flag, system count
tmvp systems [env]                # name, type, labels, via, login state (never secrets)
tmvp <env> <system> ls            # what exists: tables, collections, prefixes, streams, pages, apis, saved items
tmvp verbs [type]                 # every verb + mode, from the connector registry
tmvp llms [topic] | --full        # these docs
tmvp <any command> --llmhelp      # agent help for that exact command (works without config/server)
```
Do NOT pre-write schemas into a skill: ask the system with `ls`, `describe`, `collections`.

## Grammar
```
tmvp [envsel] <system> <verb> [args]      envsel: prod | prod,staging | all | 'prod*'  (omitted = all)
tmvp <env.system> <verb> [args]           prod.db | 'prod.*' | '*.db'
tmvp <envsel> <verb> -l role=primary      every system matching the labels
tmvp [envsel] <system> @name [args]       run a saved item (the type's @item verb)
tmvp write <env> <system> <verb|stmt> [args] --reason "…" [--preview]
```
Global flags: `--skill <dir>`, `--config <file>`, `--json` (JSONL frames), `--diff`, `--limit N`,
`--since 1h`, `--reason "…"`, `-l k=v`, `--timeout 60s`, `-F key=value` (connector flags),
`--llmhelp`.

## Output
Rows are printed as `env.system  k=v  k=v`; with `--json` every line is a frame
`{"type":"row|text|status|error|info","env":…,"system":…,"row":{…}}`. Some envs failing →
exit 4 (`partial`) with the other envs' results still printed. See `tmvp llms errors`.

Topics: install, config, writes, errors, server, skills, troubleshooting, and one per type
(`tmvp llms postgres`, `tmvp llms web`, …).


---
<!-- docs/llms/install.md -->

# Install tmvp

One static binary per OS/arch (macOS, Linux, Windows; amd64 + arm64; `CGO_ENABLED=0`). Install it
once per machine; every product skill on the machine shares it and its warm local server.

```
go install github.com/muthuishere/tmvp/cmd/tmvp@latest      # from source (Go 1.26)
# or in a checkout:
task build        # → bin/tmvp
task cross        # all 6 OS/arch builds → dist/
tmvp version      # version, protocol, registered connector types
```

External CLIs are only needed for the types that drive them, resolved from PATH:
`aws` (aws), `gcloud` (gcp), `az` (az), `git` (git), `playwright-cli` (web browser verbs:
`npm install -g @playwright/cli && playwright-cli install-browser`). Your secret manager's CLI
(`sec`, `op`, `lpass`, `gcloud`, `aws` …) runs the `$(…)` commands in config.

## First skill
```
tmvp new skill acme --systems db:postgres,cluster:k8s,admin:web --envs dev,staging,prod
# → .agents/skills/acme-tmvp/{SKILL.md, config.yaml, assets/}
# fill the $file(sec get REPLACE_ME_… --out ${out}) slots and REPLACE_ME fields, then:
tmvp --skill .agents/skills/acme-tmvp validate
tmvp --skill .agents/skills/acme-tmvp skill lint
tmvp --skill .agents/skills/acme-tmvp check
```
`tmvp skill add <name> <type> [--env prod]` adds a system later; `tmvp skill sync` regenerates
SKILL.md from config.yaml.


---
<!-- docs/llms/config.md -->

# config.yaml

Holds NO secret values — only commands that fetch them — so it lives next to the skill in git.

## Lookup order (first found wins; `--config` / `--skill` override)
1. `./.tmvp/config.yaml` (walking up from the cwd) · 2. the skill dir (`.agents/skills/<product>-tmvp/`)
3. `~/.tmvp/<product>/config.yaml` · 4. `~/.tmvp/config.yaml`. `tmvp config path` prints the pick.

## Shape
```yaml
version: 1
product: acme
assets: [assets, ../ops-repo/tmvp-assets]   # asset roots, searched in order (default [assets])
logging: { sink: file, path: ~/.tmvp/acme/logs }
server: { idle: 30m }
vars:    { region: ap-south-1 }              # ${vars.region}
secrets:                                     # named, lazy, held in server memory only
  ssh_key: "$file(sec get ACME_SSH_KEY --out ${out})"
envs:
  prod:
    destructive: false
    vars:    { domain: acme.com }            # env overrides top-level
    secrets: { db_ro: "$(op read op://Acme/prod-db/ro-dsn)" }
    systems:
      bastion:   { type: ssh, host: bastion.internal.example, user: deploy, key: "${file:secrets.ssh_key}" }
      db-tunnel: { type: portforward, via: bastion, remote: db.internal:5432 }
      db:
        type: postgres
        via: db-tunnel
        labels: { role: primary }
        read:  { dsn: "${secrets.db_ro}" }
        write: { dsn: "$file(sec get ACME_PROD_DB_RW --out ${out})" }   # inline $(…) is fine too
        limits: { rows: 500, statement_timeout: 10s }
      cloud:
        type: gcp
        project: acme-prod
        login: { manual: "gcloud auth login", check: "gcloud auth print-access-token" }
```

## Interpolation (after YAML parsing, per field — a value can never change structure)
| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `${vars.x}` | var (env vars override top-level) |
| `${secrets.x}` | named secret (env overrides top-level) |
| `${file:secrets.x}` | the secret as a FILE (whole field only): connectors get bytes in memory; external CLIs get a memfd (Linux) or 0600 temp file for that call only |
| `${NAME}` / `${NAME:-default}` | process environment variable, with default |
| `${user.x}` | left verbatim for web login steps (the named user's field) |
| `$$` | a literal `$` |

## Secrets are commands
- `"$(cmd args)"` — run (argv, no shell; `sh -c` only when it needs pipes), stdout captured in memory.
- `"$file(cmd --out ${out})"` — the command writes the private path `${out}`; tmvp reads and deletes it.
- A command may print `{"value":"…","expires_at":"RFC3339"}`; tmvp refetches before expiry.
- Run lazily on first use, held in the server's memory, redacted from all output. Refetched when the
  config changes or a credential is rejected (retried once; same value → `secret_invalid`).
- Literal values are rejected by `tmvp validate` in secret-ish fields: `dsn password passwd token key
  creds kubeconfig credentials secret uri api_key apikey private_key client_secret access_key
  secret_key`, and any URL with `user:password@`.

## Fields tmvp itself parses (per system)
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | connector type (required) — see `tmvp verbs` |
| `labels` | free `key: value`; select with `-l role=primary,team!=x`, `-l 'role in (a,b)'` |
| `via` | tunnel chain (ProxyJump semantics): `via: bastion` or `via: [jump1, db-tunnel]` — ssh, portforward or k8s systems in the same env; a docker container behind ssh: `via: [box, {container: pg}]` (`network:`, `sudo: true` optional; must follow an ssh hop, last) |
| `login` | `{manual: "<cmd the USER runs>", check: "<non-interactive cmd>"}`, or `{manual: browser}` for web |
| `destructive` | system-level override of the env flag |
| `limits` | `{rows, lines, bytes, timeout, statement_timeout, cost_per_second, rows_per_second, bytes_per_second, points_per_second, seq_scan_rows}` (defaults 1000 rows, 500 lines, 1 MiB, 10s, 15s). Also allowed at top level and per env; `timeout` precedence: `--timeout` > system > env > global > 10s — see `tmvp llms cost-and-timeouts` |
Everything else belongs to the type (`tmvp llms <type>`); `read.*` / `write.*` sub-maps hold the
credential per mode (write mode never falls back to `read.*`).

## Assets (saved items)
`assets:` lists asset roots relative to config.yaml (`~` expands). Each root holds
`<system>/<kind>/<name>.<ext>`: `queries/*.sql|*.json`, `scripts/*`, `pages/*.md` (+ `context.md`),
`apis/*.md`, `manifests/*.yaml`, `notes/`. Lookup goes root by root — the first match wins — so a
team repo can override a shared one. `tmvp <env> <system> ls` shows every item with its source file.
Every saved item starts with YAML front-matter (`description:` at least); `tmvp skill lint` checks it.

## Names
Env and system names must not contain `. , * ? [` or spaces and must not collide with each other,
with tmvp commands (`all write validate config check logs login secrets server version help new
skill export completion verbs envs systems llms`) or with a verb. `tmvp validate` reports it.


---
<!-- docs/llms/writes.md -->

# Writes & safety

tmvp trusts the agent, and makes every change explicit and traceable.

- **Reads** run on the `read:` credential in read-only sessions (pg/mysql `READ ONLY` tx, mongo
  secondary reads, k8s GET-only transport, cloud read-op allow lists). A read verb that would mutate
  → `policy_blocked` with a hint naming `tmvp write`. Make the read role unprivileged anyway: the
  session flags are defence in depth.
- **Writes**: only `tmvp write <env> <system> <verb|statement> [args] --reason "why"`.
  One env, one system, never batched. `--reason` is mandatory. `--preview` shows the blast radius
  where cheap (rolled-back transaction with rows affected, dry run, the request it would send).
- A non-verb after the system goes to the type's **default write verb**: `tmvp write prod db
  "update users set …"` → `exec`; `tmvp write prod bastion @rotate` → ssh `run @rotate`.
- **Destructive** (DROP/TRUNCATE, DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE, empty mongo filters, flushdb, purge,
  namespace delete, …) runs only where `destructive: true` (env or system).
- **read-write verbs** (web click/fill/press/select/do, cloud `call`, http `call`) run as plain
  reads only when they cannot mutate; through `tmvp write` they may.
- **Cost guard** on every read: estimated first, refused with `too_expensive` when over its timeout (`tmvp llms cost-and-timeouts`).
- **Guards** on every call: per-target timeout (always a hard kill, even with `--force`), statement timeout, row/line/byte caps, bounded
  scans/consumes/tails. Cut-offs → `guard_rejected` (exit 5) or a `truncated` status.
- **Audit**: every command is recorded (JSONL, OTel log shape) under the product's log dir;
  `tmvp logs --writes` reads the write audit back.

## Good
```
tmvp write prod db "update orders set status='paid' where id=42" --reason "support #812" --preview
tmvp write prod db "update orders set status='paid' where id=42" --reason "support #812"
tmvp write prod cluster scale deploy/api 4 --reason "traffic spike"
tmvp write prod api call refund-order id=42 --reason "support #812"
```
## Bad
- writing without the user asking; looping `tmvp write` over envs to "batch" a change
- `--reason "fix"` — say what and why; it is the audit trail
- putting the mutation in a read verb, or a secret value in an argument


---
<!-- docs/llms/code-mode.md -->

# Code mode — one program instead of many calls

`tmvp code run` takes one small JavaScript program. The program calls tmvp operations
(in parallel, in loops), works on the results, and only its final value comes back.
Every call still goes through the local tmvp server, like a CLI call.

## When to use it

- **One question, one call:** use the plain CLI. `tmvp all db query "select …" --diff`.
- **Several reads, then a comparison or a drill-down:** write one program. The raw rows stay
  inside the program; the agent gets a short summary.
- **An investigation you will run again:** save it as a script in the skill (`scripts/<name>.js`).

Check saved scripts before writing a new one: `tmvp code scripts`.

## Commands

```
tmvp code operations              # every operation: db.query, db.describe, write.db.exec, ...
tmvp code describe db.query       # input schema of one operation
tmvp code check prog.js           # diagnostics only, nothing runs (exit 2 on errors)
tmvp code run prog.js --json      # {ok, value, error, ms}
tmvp code run stuck-orders        # <skill dir>/scripts/stuck-orders.js
tmvp code scripts                 # saved scripts + first-line description
tmvp code docs                    # the language reference (supported JS subset)
```

Flags: `--json`, `--input '<json>'` (read as the global `input`), `--max-steps`,
`--max-time` (default 60s), `--concurrency` (default 4), `--max-ops` (default 200 operation
calls per program; past it the program stops, uncatchable, exit 1), `--max-memory` (default 1024 MiB; a best-effort soft Go memory limit so a
runaway program fails instead of exhausting the machine; 0 = off), `--allow-writes`.
`-e/--env` is refused: put `env` in each operation call.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the program failed, 2 nothing ran (check errors, usage).

## The API

Reads are `ops.<system>.<verb>(opts)`. Options:
`{env, args[], flags{}, labels, diff, limit, since, timeout, reason}`.
`env` takes any selector the CLI takes: `prod`, `dev,prod`, `all`, `type:prod`, `'prod*'`.
There is no `force` on reads.

A call returns `{rows, lines, targets, errors, exit}`. Every row and line carries its `env`.
A refused call throws, with the tmvp code first: `policy_blocked: …`, `too_expensive: …`.

The language is a subset of JavaScript run inside the CLI (no Node, no npm, no `new`, no
regular expressions). `tmvp code docs` lists what is supported.

## Example: compare envs, then drill into the odd one

```js
// which env has orders stuck in pending_payment, and why
const stuck = await ops.db.query({ env: "all", args: ["select count(*)::int as n from orders where status = 'pending_payment'"] })
const odd = stuck.rows.filter(r => r.n > 0).map(r => r.env)
const detail = await Promise.all(odd.map(env => Promise.all([
  ops.db.query({ env, args: ["select status_code, error, count(*)::int as n from webhook_events where status_code <> 200 group by 1, 2"] }),
  ops.app.run({ env, args: ["@logs", "1h"] }),
])))
export default odd.map((env, i) => ({
  env,
  stuck: stuck.rows.find(r => r.env === env).n,
  webhooks: detail[i][0].rows,
  log_errors: detail[i][1].lines.filter(l => l.text.indexOf(" 500") >= 0).length,
}))
```

```
tmvp code run prog.js --json
```

## Saved scripts in the repo

Saved scripts live in the skill: `<skill dir>/scripts/<name>.js`. The first `//` line is the
description shown by `tmvp code scripts`. Run one by name: `tmvp code run <name>`, with
`--input '{"env":"prod"}'` for parameters. `tmvp new skill` scaffolds `scripts/example.js`.

Commit them with the skill. They hold no secrets: credentials stay in `config.yaml` as secret
references, resolved by the server.

## Writes

Writes are `ops.write.<system>.<verb>({env, args, reason, preview, force})` (operation name `write.<system>.<verb>`).

- Refused unless the run has `--allow-writes`.
- `reason` is required.
- The server still enforces one env per write, `force` on protected envs, and the audit log
  (`tmvp logs --writes`).

```js
const r = await ops.write.db.exec({ env: "staging", args: ["update orders set status = 'paid' where id = 42"], reason: "support #812", preview: true })
```

## Safety: the server is still the gate

A program can do nothing a CLI call could not. Reads are read-only sessions, the cost guard
(`too_expensive`), timeouts, row caps, env-type protection and the audit log all apply to every
call. `--max-steps`, `--max-time`, `--max-ops` and `--max-memory` bound the program itself; a
per-call `timeout` above `--max-time` is refused (`policy_blocked`), so a program cannot raise
the cost-guard ceiling past its own budget. Strings are capped at 64 MiB and arrays at 10M
elements (the run stops). Imports are confined to the script's directory, symlinks resolved.

## Benchmark

acme demo (`examples/agent-benchmark`), warm server, median of 7, bytes of `--json` output:

| Investigation | One program | Separate calls |
|---|---|---|
| Stuck orders | 618 B, 83 ms | 3,245 B, 112 ms (3 calls) |
| Missed migration | 428 B, 167 ms | 70,554 B, 291 ms |
| Trailing space | 1,033 B, 172 ms | 172,499 B, 187 ms |


---
<!-- docs/llms/errors.md -->

# Errors & exit codes

Errors print as `error: <code>: <message> (hint: …)`; with `--json` as
`{"type":"error","error":{"code":…,"message":…,"hint":…}}`. Messages never contain secret values.

| Code | Exit | Meaning / what to do |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime` | 1 | unexpected failure; read the message |
| `timeout` | 1 | hard timeout hit (also with `--force`); narrow the query or raise `--timeout` / `limits.timeout` |
| `unreachable` | 1 | cannot connect (host down, VPN, tunnel); `tmvp check`, `tmvp <env> <tunnel> status` |
| `auth_error` | 1 | credential rejected; tmvp already refetched secrets and retried once |
| `unsupported` | 1 | missing CLI (aws/gcloud/az/git/playwright-cli) or feature |
| `config_error` | 2 | bad config; `tmvp validate` |
| `usage` | 2 | bad arguments; `<command> --llmhelp` |
| `not_found` | 2 | no such env/system/verb/saved item/api; `tmvp systems`, `… ls` |
| `secret_missing` | 2 | a `$(…)` command failed for that slot (no access); other systems still work |
| `secret_invalid` | 2 | refetched value was rejected again; ask the user to rotate/fix access |
| `login_required` | 2 | manual login needed — SHOW THE USER the command in the hint, they run it, then retry |
| `policy_blocked` | 3 | read-only violation, missing `--reason`, destructive not allowed, multi-target write |
| `too_expensive` | 3 | the read's estimate exceeds its timeout; it did not run. Narrow the query, or `--timeout <dur>`, or `--force` (`tmvp llms cost-and-timeouts`) |
| `partial` | 4 | some envs failed; the rest of the results were printed |
| `guard_rejected` | 5 | a guard cut it off (statement timeout, scan limit, byte cap) |


---
<!-- docs/llms/server.md -->

# The local server

One binary, two roles. Every `tmvp` call is a thin client that talks over a unix socket to a
per-user server which it auto-starts (detached) when needed. The server keeps per-product state:
secrets (memory only), connection pools, tunnels, browser sessions, the audit writer.

- `tmvp server status` — loaded products, connections, tunnels, secret slots (names only)
- `tmvp server stop` — drop everything (all secrets and connections); `start` / `run` (foreground)
- `tmvp secrets reload` — rerun the secret commands after a rotation; `tmvp secrets clear`
- Idle shutdown after 30 min without a request (`server: { idle: 30m }` or `TMVP_IDLE`).
- Config file changes are picked up on the next call (changed secrets refetched, affected pools rebuilt).
- Socket `~/.tmvp/run/tmvp.sock` (0600, same-UID peers only; named-pipe fallback on old Windows).

Environment: `TMVP_HOME` (state dir, default `~/.tmvp`), `TMVP_SOCKET` (socket path; keep it
under 104 bytes on macOS), `TMVP_NO_SERVER=1` (run in-process, no socket — tests/CI),
`TMVP_PRODUCT` (product for the lookup order), `TMVP_AGENT` (agent name in the audit).
Commands that never need the server or a config: `--llmhelp`, `llms`, `verbs`, `version`,
`new skill`, `skill lint`.


---
<!-- docs/llms/skills.md -->

# Building a skill on tmvp

A product skill is tiny and generated: `SKILL.md` is rendered from `config.yaml` by
`tmvp new skill` / `tmvp skill add` / `tmvp skill sync` (product, envs, systems, rules, and how to
learn the rest from tmvp). Everything else is discovered live or saved by people as assets.

## Layout
```
.agents/skills/acme-tmvp/
├── SKILL.md         # generated — do not hand-edit (sync rewrites it)
├── config.yaml      # envs → systems; $(…) secret commands; assets: [roots…]
└── assets/<system>/{queries,scripts,pages,apis,manifests,notes}/
```
Assets can come from several repos: `assets: [assets, ../platform/tmvp-assets]`. People keep adding
to them; first match wins; `ls` shows each item's source.

## Saved items — front-matter first, then the body
```sql
/*---
description: paid orders without an invoice (last N days)
params: [days]
---*/
select id, total from orders where status='paid' and invoice_id is null
  and created_at > now() - ($1 || ' days')::interval
```
```markdown
---
method: GET
path: /api/orders/{id}
description: one order with lines
params: [id]
mutating: false
---
Returns 404 for archived orders.
```
ssh scripts declare `read: true` in front-matter; `script` type uses a `# tmvp: read` header.

## Good practice
- Let the agent discover: `tmvp envs`, `tmvp systems`, `tmvp all db ls`, `tmvp prod db describe orders`.
- Save a query/script/api only after it proved useful; give it a precise `description`.
- Keep notes short and factual in `assets/<system>/notes/` (gotchas, env differences).
- Run `tmvp skill lint` before committing (structure, front-matter, no secret values).

## Bad practice
- Pre-writing table lists, schemas or endpoints from guesses — they rot. References must come from the code and be confirmed by live `ls`/`describe`; `ls` stays the source of truth.
- Putting values in config (`password: hunter2`) — use `$(command)`; lint/validate reject literals.
- Copying one product's systems into another skill — one skill = one product.
- Saved items that mutate without saying so (mark `mutating: true`, or omit `read: true`).


---
<!-- docs/llms/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Do |
|---|---|
| `no config found` | pass `--skill <dir>` or `--config <file>`; `tmvp config path` |
| `"x" is neither an env nor a system` | `tmvp envs`, `tmvp systems` |
| `unreachable` | VPN/tunnel? `tmvp <env> <tunnel> status`; `tmvp check <env> <system>` |
| `secret_missing` | the `$(…)` command failed for you (no access/not logged in to the vault); fix access, `tmvp secrets reload` |
| `login_required` | show the user the hint's command (e.g. `! gcloud auth login`, `tmvp login prod admin`), then retry |
| `unsupported … not on PATH` | install the CLI (aws, gcloud, az, git, playwright-cli) |
| `policy_blocked` | it mutates: use `tmvp write <env> <system> … --reason "…"` if the user asked |
| `guard_rejected` / truncated | narrow the query, add filters, `--limit`, or raise `limits:` |
| stale results after editing config | the server reloads on the next call; force with `tmvp server stop` |
| saved item not found | `tmvp <env> <system> ls` shows which asset roots/items exist |
| everything slow on first call | cold start: secrets run + connections open once, then warm |

`tmvp check` validates the config, resolves secrets (names only) and connects to every selected
system. `tmvp validate` and `tmvp skill lint` never run a secret command.


---
<!-- docs/llms/doctor.md -->

# tmvp doctor

One screen answering: what is installed, what can I connect to, what is broken. Works without a
config (machine, tools and types only). Runs in-process — it never starts the server — and reports
secret **names and states only**, never values or the commands that produce them.

```
tmvp doctor                                   # everything; config by lookup order if one exists
tmvp doctor --offline                         # no secret commands, login checks or connections
tmvp --skill .agents/skills/acme-tmvp doctor --env prod --system db
tmvp doctor --json                            # JSONL rows, each with "section"
```

Sections:

| Section | Shows |
|---|---|
| machine | tmvp version, OS/arch, `TMVP_HOME`, socket path + length check, server (pid, uptime, product names) |
| tools | kubectl (optional), aws, gcloud, az, git, playwright-cli, and secret sources (sec, op, lpass, vault): found?, `--version` first line, which types need it; binaries the config's `$(…)` commands run are flagged when missing |
| types | every registered type with read / write verb counts and whether it is built-in |
| config / systems | per env × system: type known, secrets (ok / missing / invalid / unknown), login (ok / required + the command), via chain, connect (ok / failed + code) |
| summary | problem count and the top 3 fixes with exact commands |

Exit codes: `0` all good · `1` something failing (missing tool the config needs, login required,
secret or connection failed) · `2` config problem (no/invalid config given, validation errors,
unknown type).

Fixes it suggests: `install playwright-cli: npm i -g @playwright/cli`, `install aws`,
`run: gcloud auth login` (the system's `login.manual`), `set TMVP_SOCKET …`, `tmvp validate`.
Use `tmvp check` for the server-side view (warm pools, cached secrets).


---
<!-- docs/llms/environments.md -->

# Environments — which env a command runs on

## Selection precedence (first wins)

| # | Source | How | `env_source` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | positional selector or `--env/-e` | `tmvp prod db ls`, `tmvp prod.db ls`, `tmvp -e prod db ls` | `explicit` |
| 2 | `TMVP_ENV` | `export TMVP_ENV=staging` (one shell) | `TMVP_ENV` |
| 3 | `tmvp use <env>` | persisted per product + config path | `use` |
| 4 | `default_env:` in config.yaml | `default_env: dev` (top level) | `default` |
| 5 | nothing set | the **first env** in config.yaml (`tmvp all …` for every env) | `default` |

Giving the env both positionally and with `-e` (different values) is a usage error.

## `tmvp use`

```
tmvp use            # print the active env and where it came from
tmvp use dev        # persist dev for this product (TMVP_HOME/state/env.json, 0600)
tmvp use prod       # allowed for any env; writes to prod still need --force
tmvp use default    # forget it → default_env, else the first env (same as --clear)
```

The state is keyed by the canonical config path + product name, so two
configs naming the same product never share a choice.

## Batch is still first-class

Name several envs and the same read runs on all of them in parallel:
`tmvp all db ls`, `tmvp dev,prod db query "select 1" --diff`, `tmvp 'prod*' db health`,
`tmvp '*.db' health`, `tmvp prod -l role=primary health`. An explicit selector always
wins over `use`/default_env.

## Output says where the env came from

- text mode: a header on stderr — `# env: dev (source: use — tmvp use (…/env.json))`
- `--json`: every frame carries `env` and `env_source`
- the audit log records `env_source`, `env_selector` and `force` on every command and write

## Writes and `--force`

Writes run on exactly one env and one system (never batched). A **protected** env —
`destructive: false`, the default, i.e. production — needs `--force` in addition to
`--reason`, however the env was chosen (named, `-e`, `TMVP_ENV`, `use`, `default_env`).
`--preview` needs no `--force` (it changes nothing).

```
tmvp write prod db "update …" --reason "fix #42" --preview
tmvp write prod db "update …" --reason "fix #42" --force
tmvp use dev && tmvp write db "update …" --reason "test data"   # dev has destructive: true
```

## Names

An env named like a system, a verb or a tmvp command (`use`, `certs`, …) is rejected by
`tmvp validate`, so `tmvp <word> …` is never ambiguous. `default_env` must name an env.

## Env types — many envs of one kind

```yaml
envs:
  dev-alice: { type: dev }          # dev/test/local: destructive allowed by default
  staging:   { type: staging }      # staging and untyped envs: protected by default
  prod-eu:   { type: production }   # prod: always protected; destructive: true is rejected
  prod-us:   { type: production }
```
`type:` accepts common spellings and normalises them: production/prod/prd/live → `prod`; staging/stage/stg/uat/preprod/qa → `staging`; development/develop/dev → `dev`; test/testing/ci → `test`; `local`. Any other word is kept as a custom type. An explicit `destructive:` wins, except on a prod-type env.

Select by type: `tmvp type:prod db query "select 1"`, or the bare type word when no env has that name (`tmvp prod db …` reads prod-eu and prod-us). Writes still take exactly one env.


---
<!-- docs/llms/secrets.md -->

# Secrets & certificates — health

Secrets are `$(command)`s run lazily by the local server and held in memory only
(see `tmvp llms config`). These commands report on them **without ever printing a
value or key material**.

## `tmvp secrets status [-e envsel] [--days 30]`

Fetches every secret in scope (top-level + the selected envs; all envs without `-e`)
and prints one row per name:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `ok` · `missing` (command failed / printed nothing) · `invalid` (rejected / too short) · `login_required` (a system using it fails its `login.check`) |
| `source` | the first word of the command only (`sec`, `op`, `aws` …); `env` for `${VAR}` secrets |
| `fetched_at` | last fetch by this server |
| `updated` | `yes`/`no`: the value changed since the previous fetch (compared by a salted hash kept in server memory, never the value); `unknown` on the first fetch |
| `expires_at` | when the command printed `{"value":…,"expires_at":…}` |
| `cert_*` | for PEM / kubeconfig (`client-certificate-data`, embedded PEM) / service-account JSON: earliest x509 `NotAfter`, days left, subject, count, `ok`/`expiring`/`expired` |
| `private_key` | whether a private key is present (`true`/`false`; never the key) |

Exit 2 when any secret is not ok, 1 when a held cert is expired.

## `tmvp secrets audit [--since 1d]`

From the audit log: every `fetch`, `refresh`, `invalidate` (after an auth error) and
`failure`, per name, with time, the command that triggered it (`run prod.db query`) and
`updated`. No values.

## `tmvp certs [-e envsel] [--days 30]`

TLS handshake (read-only, 5s timeout, through `via:` tunnels) with every system that has
a TLS endpoint, plus certs held in secrets:

- postgres: DSN with `sslmode=require|verify-ca|verify-full` (SSLRequest, then TLS)
- `https://` `url`/`base_url` (http, web, prometheus, elasticsearch, grafana, loki …)
- k8s: the API server of the kubeconfig `context`
- `rediss://`, `tls://`, `wss://`, `mongodb…?tls=true`; `host`/`brokers` with `tls: true` or `security_protocol: SSL`

Per endpoint: leaf `NotAfter`, days left (`chain_min_days` over the chain), issuer, SANs,
trusted (system roots). `expiring` when < `--days`; exit 1 when anything is expired or
unreachable.

## `tmvp doctor`

The summary adds two lines — `secrets:` (ok / missing / certs expiring) and
`certificates:` (endpoints expiring within 30 days) — and the top fixes name them.

## `$dotenv(file, KEY)` — use the .env files you already have
```yaml
envs:
  prod:
    secrets:
      pg_pw: "$dotenv(.env.prod, PGPASSWORD)"   # see path rules below
```
Paths: `.env.prod` = repo root (falls back to the config's folder if not there); `./x` or `../x` = relative to config.yaml; `/abs/path`, `C:\…`, `\\server\share\…` and `~/…` as written. `/` and `\` both work as separators on every OS, so one config.yaml works on macOS, Linux and Windows.
tmvp's local server reads just that key (dotenv rules: `export`, quotes, `# comments`, last definition wins) and keeps the value in memory — the agent only ever sees the file and key names. A missing file, missing or empty key is `secret_missing`, naming file and key, never a value. `tmvp env-keys` lists the keys each env file has.
The value still sits in a plain-text file on disk: fine to start; for prod, prefer `$file(sec get … --out ${out})` (encrypted, unreadable even with `cat`).

## `${VAR}` — process environment
`pg_pw: "${PGPASSWORD}"` (or `${PGPASSWORD:-default}`) reads the variable from the **tmvp server's** environment, i.e. the shell that first started it (`tmvp server stop` after changing the variable). Good for CI; for laptops prefer `$dotenv(…)` or `sec`, which don't depend on which terminal started the server.


---
<!-- docs/llms/logs-and-metrics.md -->

# logs and metrics — where to query

OpenTelemetry has no query endpoint of its own: the collector *exports* to a backend, and you query
the backend. Find where your logs/metrics/traces land (the collector's `exporters:`), then use that type.

| Where it lands | tmvp type | Verb |
|---|---|---|
| Loki (logs) | `loki` | `range '{app="api"} \|= "error"' --since 30m`, `tail`, `query` (metric LogQL) |
| Prometheus / Mimir / Thanos / VictoriaMetrics (metrics) | `prometheus` | `query`, `range`, `alerts` |
| Elasticsearch / OpenSearch (logs, APM) | `elasticsearch` / `opensearch` | `search <index> '<json>'`, `count` |
| Anything Grafana can see (incl. Tempo-less OTel backends) | `grafana` | `query <datasource-uid> '<expr>'`, `dashboard <uid>` to copy a panel's query |
| GCP Cloud Logging | `gcp` | `logs` |
| AWS CloudWatch Logs | `aws` | `logs` |
| Azure Monitor / Log Analytics | `az` | `logs` |
| Pod stdout (no backend) | `k8s` | `logs` |
| Plain files on a VM | `ssh` | `@script` (e.g. `journalctl`/`tail` in a saved script) |

Tips:
- Always narrow first: `loki values app`, `prometheus ls http_`, `elasticsearch mapping <index>`, `grafana ls`.
- Every read is bounded (`--since`, `--limit`, byte cap); ask for less and repeat rather than one huge pull.
- Multi-env: `tmvp all logs range '{app="api"} |= "panic"' --since 1h` runs per env in parallel.

<!-- docs/llms/types/aws.md -->

# aws

AWS through the `aws` CLI with a per-call environment (your ~/.aws is never modified).

## Fields
region, profile, access_key/secret_key/session_token (secrets), credentials/config (`${file:secrets.x}`); login: {manual: "aws sso login --profile p", check: "aws sts get-caller-identity --profile p"}

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — configured scope (profile, region), whoami, saved scripts |
| `whoami` | read | sts get-caller-identity (account, arn) |
| `logs` | read | logs <log-group> [filter-pattern] — CloudWatch, bounded by --since (≤7d) / --limit |
| `call` | read-write | call <service> <op> [args] — read-only ops; through tmvp write any op (--preview shows it) |
| `cli` | write, default | alias of `call` for tmvp write (kept for compatibility) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = configured scope (profile, region) + saved scripts + whoami.

## Examples
```
tmvp all aws ls
tmvp prod aws logs /ecs/api "ERROR" --since 1h
tmvp prod aws call ec2 describe-instances
tmvp write prod aws call ec2 start-instances --instance-ids i-0abc --reason "restore box"
```

# az

Azure through `az`; a service principal runs in a private AZURE_CONFIG_DIR per call.

## Fields
subscription, tenant/client_id/client_secret (secret) or certificate, workspace; login: {manual: "az login", check: "az account show"}

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — configured scope (subscription, resource_group, workspace, tenant), whoami, saved scripts |
| `whoami` | read | az account show (subscription, tenant, user) |
| `logs` | read | logs ["<kql>"] — Log Analytics (workspace:) or, without a query, the activity log; bounded by --since (≤7d) / --limit |
| `call` | read-write | call <az args> — read commands only (list/show/query ...); through tmvp write any call (--preview shows it) |
| `cli` | write, default | alias of `call` for tmvp write (kept for compatibility) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = configured scope (subscription, resource_group, workspace, tenant) + saved scripts + whoami.

## Examples
```
tmvp all azure ls
tmvp prod azure logs "AppRequests | take 20"
tmvp prod azure call vm list
tmvp write prod azure call vm start -n api -g rg --reason "restore"
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/elasticsearch.md -->

# elasticsearch

Elasticsearch and OpenSearch (type `elasticsearch` or its alias `opensearch`; same verbs). Plain HTTP, no SDK. A read connection only sends GET, plus POST to `_search`, `_count`, `_msearch`, `_mapping`, `_field_caps`, `_validate/query`.

## Fields
url (or base_url), one of api_key (`Authorization: ApiKey …`) | token (bearer) | user/password, headers, ca (`${file:secrets.ca}`), insecure; per mode. 401 → `auth_error`; 403 → `policy_blocked` (the credential lacks the privilege).

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [substring] — indices (health, docs), aliases, saved queries/*.json |
| `health` | read | health — cluster health (status, nodes, shards) |
| `indices` | read | indices [pattern] — _cat/indices (health, status, docs, size) |
| `mapping` | read | mapping <index> — one row per field: index, field (dotted), type |
| `search` | read, @item | search <index> '<json>'\|@saved [-F q=<lucene>] — hits as rows; size ≤ --limit, server timeout; @saved = queries/<name>.json (front-matter index:) |
| `count` | read | count <index> ['<json>'\|@saved] [-F q=<lucene>] |
| `cat` | read | cat <endpoint> [pattern] — allow-listed _cat endpoints: health indices aliases nodes shards allocation count segments thread_pool pending_tasks recovery templates master plugins fielddata tasks |
| `get` | read | get <index> <id> — one document |
| `index` | write, default | index <index> '<json>'\|@saved [-F id=<id>] — create/replace a document |
| `update` | write | update <index> <id> '<partial json>' — partial update (body without "doc"/"script" is wrapped in {"doc": …}) |
| `delete` | write | delete <index> <id> — delete one document |
| `update-by-query` | write | update-by-query <index> '<json with query + script>' (--preview = count; no query = every doc → needs destructive) |
| `delete-index` | destructive | delete-index <index> — no wildcards, no _all |
| `delete-by-query` | destructive | delete-by-query <index> '<json with query>' (--preview = count) |
| `reindex` | destructive | reindex '<json {"source":…,"dest":…}>' |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [substring]` = indices (non-dot), aliases and saved queries `assets/<system>/queries/<name>.json` (front-matter `index:`; `tmvp prod search @errors` runs `search`). `search` sets `size` ≤ `--limit` and a server-side `timeout`; responses are capped by `limits.bytes`.

Destructive detection: `update-by-query` without a query (or `match_all`) needs `destructive: true`; `delete-index` refuses wildcards and `_all`.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod search ls
tmvp prod search mapping logs-2026.11
tmvp all search search 'logs-*' '{"query":{"term":{"http.status":500}}}' --limit 20
tmvp prod search count orders -F q='status:failed'
tmvp prod search cat shards
tmvp write prod search index orders '{"id":1,"status":"ok"}' -F id=1 --reason "fix doc"
tmvp write prod search delete-by-query orders '{"query":{"term":{"test":true}}}' --preview --reason "drop test docs"
```

# gcp

## Fields

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — configured scope (project, region, zone, account), whoami, saved scripts |
| `whoami` | read | active account and project |
| `logs` | read | logs ["<logging filter>"] — Cloud Logging, newest first, bounded by --since (≤7d) / --limit |
| `call` | read-write | call <gcloud args> — read verbs only (list/describe/read ...); through tmvp write any call (--preview shows it) |
| `cli` | write, default | alias of `call` for tmvp write (kept for compatibility) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = configured scope (project, region, zone, account) + saved scripts + whoami.

## Examples
```

```

<!-- docs/llms/types/gh.md -->

# gh

GitHub through `gh`: workflow runs and logs, deployments, PRs, releases for one repo. tmvp sets the repo (`-R` / `GH_REPO`); a `token` goes only into the child's `GH_TOKEN`.

## Fields
repo (owner/name, required), host (GitHub Enterprise), token (secret, optional; default is the user's `gh auth login`); login: {manual: "gh auth login", check: "gh auth status"}

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — configured repo/host, whoami, saved scripts |
| `whoami` | read | the GitHub account gh is using (login, name) |
| `runs` | read | runs [--workflow W] [--branch B] [--status S] — recent workflow runs (bounded by --limit) |
| `run` | read | run <id> — one run and its jobs (status, conclusion, times) |
| `run-log` | read | run-log <id> [--failed] — the run's log (--failed: failed steps only), line-capped |
| `workflows` | read | workflows — the repo's workflows (name, path, state) |
| `prs` | read | prs [--state open\|closed\|merged\|all] — pull requests |
| `pr` | read | pr <n> — one pull request with checks and review state |
| `releases` | read | releases — tags, names, latest/draft/prerelease, dates |
| `deployments` | read | deployments [--environment E] — GitHub deployments (environment, ref, sha, creator, time) |
| `branches` | read | branches — branch names, head sha, protected |
| `call` | read-write | call <gh args> — reads only (run/pr/issue/release/workflow/label/cache list\|view\|status\|diff\|checks, api GET); through tmvp write any allowed call |
| `rerun` | write | rerun <run-id> [--failed] — re-run a workflow run (tmvp write; --preview shows it) |
| `dispatch` | write | dispatch <workflow> [--ref R] [-f k=v ...] — trigger a workflow_dispatch run (tmvp write) |
| `cancel` | write | cancel <run-id> — cancel a running workflow run (tmvp write) |
| `cli` | write, default | cli <gh args> — any gh call that is not blocked (tmvp write; --preview shows it) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Policy
- `call` runs reads only: `run|pr|issue|release|workflow|label|cache|variable|secret|repo … list|view|status|diff|checks`, and `api` GET (`-X POST`, `-f`/`-F`/`--input` without `-X GET` are writes).
- Never through tmvp, not even `tmvp write`: `auth`, `config`, `secret` (except `secret list`, names only), `ssh-key`, `gpg-key`, `extension`, `codespace`, `alias`, `gist`, `run download`, `repo delete|clone|fork|sync`, and `-R`/`--repo`/`--hostname` (set from config).
- `rerun`, `dispatch`, `cancel`, `cli` are writes: `tmvp write … --reason`, `--preview` first.

## Discovery
`ls` = configured repo/host + saved scripts + whoami. Then `workflows`, `runs`, `deployments`.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod gh runs --workflow deploy-prod-new.yml --limit 5
tmvp prod gh run 123456789
tmvp prod gh run-log 123456789 --failed
tmvp all gh deployments --environment production
tmvp prod gh call api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/main/status
tmvp write prod gh rerun 123456789 --failed --reason "flaky test" --preview
tmvp write dev gh dispatch deploy-dev-new.yml --ref main --reason "redeploy dev"
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/git.md -->

# git

Git repos, read only (never pushes). Bare clone cached per env/system, fetched at most once a minute.

## Fields
url, branch, key (`${file:secrets.x}`) or token (+ user)

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — branches and tags (kind, name, commit, date), newest first, --limit |
| `log` | read | log [rev] [-- path] — commits (hash, author, date, subject), --since / --limit |
| `diff` | read | diff [a] [b] [-- path] — default HEAD~1 HEAD; bounded text |
| `show` | read | show <rev>[:path] — commit or file at a revision; bounded text |
| `tags` | read | tags [pattern] — newest first |
| `deploys` | read | deploys [tag-pattern] — tags and commits since --since (default 7d) |
| `fetch` | read | fetch — refresh the local cache now |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = branches and tags, newest first.

## Examples
```
tmvp all infra ls --limit 20
tmvp prod infra log --since 2d
tmvp prod infra deploys
tmvp prod infra show v1.4.2:helm/values.yaml
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/grafana.md -->

# grafana

Grafana HTTP API: dashboards → the queries behind each panel, datasources, Grafana-managed alert state, annotations, and `query` on any datasource through `/api/ds/query` (Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, OTel backends — whatever Grafana can query). Writes: `annotate`, `silence create|expire`. Nothing is ever deleted.

## Fields
url (or base_url), token (service-account token: `${secrets.grafana_sa}`; Viewer for reads, Editor for annotate/silence), org_id, headers, ca, insecure. 401 → `auth_error`; 403 → `policy_blocked` (role too low).

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [substring] — dashboards (uid, folder), datasources (uid, type), saved queries/*.expr |
| `dashboards` | read | dashboards [-F q=<title search>] [-F tag=<tag>] — uid, title, folder, tags |
| `dashboard` | read | dashboard <uid> — one row per panel query: panel, title, type, datasource, ref, expr |
| `datasources` | read | datasources — uid, name, type, default |
| `alerts` | read | alerts [-F state=firing\|pending] — Grafana-managed (unified) alert instances: alert, state, severity, since, labels, summary |
| `silences` | read | silences — Grafana alertmanager silences: id, state, matchers, ends, comment |
| `annotations` | read | annotations [-F tags=a,b] [-F dashboard=<uid>] — over --since (default 24h) |
| `query` | read, @item | query <datasource-uid> '<expr>' \| query @saved — via /api/ds/query over --since (default 1h, ≤ 7d), rows capped by --limit; -F step=60s, other -F k=v go into the query object (e.g. -F queryType=range) |
| `annotate` | write, default | annotate '<text>' [-F tags=deploy,api] [-F dashboard=<uid>] [-F panel=<id>] [-F time=RFC3339] [-F end=RFC3339] |
| `silence` | write | silence create '<alertname=X,env=~prod.*>' [-F duration=1h] \| silence expire <id> — Grafana alertmanager (comment = --reason) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [substring]` = dashboards (uid) + datasources (uid, type) + saved `assets/<system>/queries/<name>.expr` (front-matter `datasource: <uid>`, body = expression; `tmvp prod grafana @name` runs `query`). `dashboard <uid>` shows the exact query each panel runs — paste it into `query`.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod grafana ls latency
tmvp prod grafana dashboard abc123
tmvp prod grafana query prom1 'sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m]))' --since 6h -F step=1m
tmvp prod grafana query loki1 '{app="api"} |= "error"' -F queryType=range --limit 50
tmvp prod grafana alerts -F state=firing
tmvp write prod grafana annotate "deploy api v2.3" -F tags=deploy,api --reason "deploy marker"
tmvp write prod grafana silence create 'alertname=HighErr,env=prod' -F duration=1h --reason "planned failover"
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/grpc.md -->

# grpc

gRPC services, with no generated code. Methods and messages come from server reflection, or from a descriptor set (`protoset:`) when the server has no reflection. Requests and responses are JSON (protojson). A method runs as a read only if it matches `read_methods`, and never if it streams from the client. Everything else runs only through `tmvp write` (`--preview` shows the request and sends nothing).

## Fields
address (`host:port`, required) · tls (`true` = TLS; default plaintext) · ca (`${file:secrets.ca}`) · server_name · insecure (skip TLS verify, test servers only) · token (secret, sent as `authorization: Bearer …` metadata) · headers (map of metadata; values may be secrets) · protoset (descriptor set file relative to the skill: `buf build -o api.binpb` or `protoc --include_imports --descriptor_set_out=api.binpb …`) · read_methods (globs on `pkg.Service/Method` or the bare method name; default `Get* List* Search* Find* Count* Describe* Check Watch Health*`) · `via:` for tunnels

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — saved calls (@name), then services and methods with kind (read/write) and streaming |
| `describe` | read | describe <service\|pkg.Service/Method\|message> — methods, or request/response fields |
| `health` | read | health [service] — grpc.health.v1 Check (status, latency) |
| `call` | read-write, default, @item | call <pkg.Service/Method> ['<json>'] \| call @saved [k=v ...] — read methods only as reads; others via tmvp write (--preview) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` lists saved calls (`assets/<system>/calls/*.json`), then every service method with kind (read/write), streaming (unary/server/client/bidi) and request/response types. `describe <service|pkg.Service/Method|message>` shows the fields.

## Saved calls
```json
---
description: one order by id
method: shop.v1.OrderService/GetOrder
params: [id]
---
{"id": "{id}"}
```
Run with `tmvp prod api @get-order id=42`, or with positional values in `params` order (`@get-order 42`).

## Examples
```
tmvp prod api ls
tmvp prod api describe shop.v1.OrderService/GetOrder
tmvp all api health
tmvp all api call shop.v1.OrderService/GetOrder '{"id":"42"}' --diff
tmvp prod api call shop.v1.OrderService/ListOrders '{"status":"PAID"}' --limit 20
tmvp write prod api call shop.v1.OrderService/CancelOrder '{"id":"42"}' --reason "support #812" --preview
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/http.md -->

# http

Plain HTTP APIs. Paths resolve against base_url (absolute URLs refused). Named APIs come from `apis/*.md` front-matter {method, path, description, params, mutating} and/or an `openapi:` file/path/URL.

## Fields
base_url, token (secret bearer) or user/password, headers, health_path, insecure, openapi (file relative to the skill, path on base_url, or URL)

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — defined APIs (assets apis/*.md + openapi:): name, method, path, mutating, source; offline unless openapi is a URL |
| `apis` | read | apis [filter] — same as ls, filtered by name/path substring |
| `call` | read-write, @item | call <api\|@api> [k=v ...] — run a defined API; {k} fills path params; mutating APIs only via tmvp write (--preview) |
| `get` | read | get <path> [-F q.key=value] [-F h.Header=value] — JSON → rows, else text |
| `health` | read | health [path] — status, latency (default health_path or /health) |
| `post` | write, default | post <path> [body] (tmvp write) |
| `put` | write | put <path> [body] (tmvp write) |
| `patch` | write | patch <path> [body] (tmvp write) |
| `delete` | write | delete <path> (tmvp write) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` / `apis [filter]` = defined APIs (offline unless openapi is a URL); `call <api>` runs GET APIs as reads, mutating ones only via tmvp write.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod api ls
tmvp all api call @get-order id=42
tmvp prod api get /v1/status -F q.verbose=1
tmvp write prod api call refund-order id=42 --reason "support #812" --preview
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/k8s.md -->

# k8s

Kubernetes via client-go (no kubectl), dialing through `via:`. Read connections refuse every non-GET request. (Being rewritten; `ls` is pending.)

## Fields
kubeconfig (`${file:secrets.x}`, read./write. override), context, namespace (`-F ns=x` per call)

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | what exists: saved manifests, then namespaces and workloads/services in the namespace (-F A=true for all) |
| `ctx` | read | context, cluster, namespace, auth kind |
| `health` | read | version, readyz, ready nodes, latency |
| `get` | read | get <kind> [name] [-F selector=app=x] [-F ns=x\|-F A=true] [-F o=yaml] |
| `describe` | read | describe <kind> <name> \| <kind>/<name> — object + its events |
| `logs` | read | logs <pod>\|deploy/<name> [-F container=c] [-F previous=true] (bounded tail, --since) |
| `events` | read | events [name] [-F type=Warning] (--since filters) |
| `top` | read | top pods\|nodes (metrics API) |
| `apply` | write, default | apply '<yaml>'\|@manifest (server-side apply; --preview = dry-run) |
| `scale` | write | scale <kind>/<name> <replicas> |
| `restart` | write | restart deploy\|sts\|ds/<name> (rollout restart) |
| `rollout` | write | rollout undo deploy/<name> [-F to-revision=N] |
| `delete` | write | delete <kind> <name> \| <kind> -F selector=… (destructive) \| ns <name> (destructive) |
| `exec` | write | exec <pod> [-F container=c] -- <cmd> [args...] |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
TODO: `ls` (namespaces/workloads) pending the client-go rewrite; until then `get ns`, `get deploy`.

## Port-forward (k8s as a `via:` hop)
A k8s system is also a tunnel: a `portforward` system with `via: <k8s system>` and
`target: kind/name:port` port-forwards (like `kubectl port-forward`) through the API server, and
any system can then use that portforward as its `via:`. `kind` is `pod`, `svc`, `deploy`, `sts`, …;
`svc/` and workload targets resolve to a Running+Ready, non-terminating pod (error `not_found` if
none); a service port maps to its `targetPort`, named ports resolve from the pod spec. The tunnel
connection is read-only except the port-forward upgrade itself. Chains work: the k8s system can
itself sit behind `via: <ssh>`.
```yaml
bastion:  { type: ssh, host: bastion.example.com, user: deploy, key: "${file:secrets.ssh_key}" }
cluster:  { type: k8s, via: bastion, kubeconfig: "${file:secrets.kubeconfig}", context: prod }
pg-fwd:   { type: portforward, via: cluster, target: svc/postgres:5432, namespace: data }
db:       { type: postgres, via: pg-fwd, read: { dsn: "${secrets.db_ro}" } }
api-fwd:  { type: portforward, via: cluster, target: deploy/api:http }
api:      { type: http, via: api-fwd, base_url: "http://api.internal" }
```
`tmvp prod db …` and `tmvp prod api get /health` then run through ssh → API server → pod.
`tmvp prod pg-fwd open` keeps a local 127.0.0.1 listener for plain psql.

## Examples
```
tmvp all cluster get pods
tmvp prod cluster logs deploy/api --since 15m --limit 200
tmvp prod cluster events
tmvp write prod cluster restart deploy/api --reason "stuck workers"
```


---
<!-- docs/llms/types/kafka.md -->

# kafka

Apache Kafka (also Redpanda, MSK, Confluent, Event Hubs' Kafka endpoint). Embedded franz-go — no CLI. Every broker connection goes through `via:`. `consume` reads partitions directly: it never joins a consumer group and never commits.

## Fields
brokers (`"b1:9092,b2:9092"`, or a YAML list of literal host:port), sasl `{mechanism: plain|scram-sha-256|scram-sha-512, user, password: ${secrets.x}}`, tls (`true`, or `{ca: ${file:secrets.ca}, cert: ${file:…}, key: ${file:…}, server_name, insecure}`); per mode (`read.sasl`, `write.sasl`). A rejected SASL credential → `auth_error` (secrets re-fetched, retried once).

```yaml
bus:
  type: kafka
  brokers: "${vars.kafka}"
  tls: true
  read:  {sasl: {mechanism: scram-sha-512, user: reader, password: "${secrets.kafka_ro}"}}
  write: {sasl: {mechanism: scram-sha-512, user: ops,    password: "${secrets.kafka_rw}"}}
```

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [substring] — topics (partitions) + saved messages/*.json |
| `topics` | read | topics [substring] — topics with partition count, replication factor |
| `describe` | read | describe <topic> — per-partition leader/replicas/isr/start/end offsets, then non-default topic configs |
| `groups` | read | groups — consumer groups (state, protocol type) |
| `lag` | read | lag <group> — per topic/partition committed offset, end offset, lag, member |
| `consume` | read | consume <topic> [-F from=earliest\|latest-N\|<offset>\|<RFC3339>] [-F partition=N] [-F wait=10s] — bounded by --limit and time; never joins a group or commits (default from=latest-10 per partition) |
| `health` | read | health — brokers, controller, cluster id |
| `produce` | write, default | produce <topic> <value\|@saved> [-F key=k] [-F partition=N] (--preview shows the record) |
| `create-topic` | write | create-topic <topic> [-F partitions=1] [-F replication=-1] [-F config.<k>=<v>] |
| `delete-topic` | destructive | delete-topic <topic> |
| `delete-records` | destructive | delete-records <topic> -F before=<offset>\|latest [-F partition=N] — truncate partitions before an offset |
| `reset-offsets` | destructive | reset-offsets <group> <topic> -F to=earliest\|latest\|<RFC3339> — group must be empty (--preview shows old→new) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [substring]` = topics + saved messages (`assets/<system>/messages/<name>.json`, used by `produce <topic> @name`).

## Examples
```
tmvp all bus ls orders
tmvp prod bus describe orders
tmvp prod bus lag billing-worker
tmvp prod bus consume orders -F from=latest-20 --limit 50
tmvp prod bus consume orders -F from=2026-11-11T09:00:00Z -F partition=3
tmvp write prod bus produce orders '{"id":1}' -F key=1 --reason "replay order 1"
tmvp write prod bus reset-offsets billing-worker orders -F to=2026-11-11T09:00:00Z --preview --reason "reprocess"
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/loki.md -->

# loki

Grafana Loki (logs). Read only. Every query needs a real label selector: `{}`, `{app=""}` or `{app=~".*"}` alone are refused (`guard_rejected`) before Loki sees them.

## Fields
url (or base_url, the Loki root — no `/loki/api`), token (bearer) or user/password (basic; Grafana Cloud = instance id + API token), tenant (`X-Scope-OrgID`), headers, ca, insecure, max_range (default `7d`).

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [substring] — label names (over --since, default 6h) + saved queries/*.logql |
| `labels` | read | labels — label names seen in --since (default 6h) |
| `values` | read | values <label> — values of a label in --since (default 6h) |
| `query` | read | query '<logql>' [-F time=RFC3339] — instant query (metric LogQL → one row per series) |
| `range` | read, @item | range '<logql>'\|@saved — log lines (newest first) or metric samples over --since (default 1h, ≤ max_range 7d); lines capped by --limit; -F step=1m -F direction=forward |
| `tail` | read | tail '<logql>'\|@saved [-F follow=10s] — last lines of --since (default 15m) oldest→newest; follow polls for new lines, bounded by time and --limit |
| `series` | read | series '<selector>' — label sets of matching streams in --since (default 1h) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = label names + saved LogQL `assets/<system>/queries/<name>.logql` (`tmvp prod logs @errors` runs `range`). Then `values <label>` to build a selector.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod logs ls
tmvp prod logs values app
tmvp all logs range '{app="api"} |= "error"' --since 30m --limit 100
tmvp prod logs query 'sum by (app) (rate({env="prod"} |= "error" [5m]))'
tmvp prod logs tail '{app="api"}' -F follow=15s
tmvp prod logs @errors --since 2h
```

# mongo

MongoDB. Reads use secondaryPreferred, `maxTimeMS` and a document cap; `$out`/`$merge` refused in reads. Filters/pipelines are relaxed Extended JSON, inline or `@saved` (`queries/*.json`).

## Fields
read.uri / write.uri (secret mongodb:// URI), database (or in the URI path); `-F db=x` per call

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [db] — saved queries (@name, all asset roots) then live collections/views |
| `collections` | read | collections [db] → collection names and types |
| `find` | read | find <coll> ['{filter}'\|@saved] [-F projection='{..}' -F sort='{..}' -F skip=N] |
| `aggregate` | read | aggregate <coll> '[pipeline]'\|@saved ($out/$merge refused: use aggregate-out) |
| `count` | read | count <coll> ['{filter}'\|@saved] |
| `insert` | write | insert <coll> '{doc}'\|'[docs]'\|@saved |
| `update` | write | update <coll> '{filter}' '{update}' (updateMany; empty filter = destructive) |
| `delete` | write | delete <coll> '{filter}' (deleteMany; empty filter = destructive) |
| `aggregate-out` | write | aggregate-out <coll> '[pipeline with $out/$merge]'\|@saved |
| `drop` | destructive | drop <coll> (destructive) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [db]` = saved queries + live collections and views.

## Examples
```
tmvp all docs ls
tmvp prod docs find users '{"email":"a@b.test"}' -F projection='{"_id":1}'
tmvp prod docs count orders '{"status":"open"}'
tmvp write prod docs update users '{"_id":"x"}' '{"$set":{"blocked":true}}' --reason "abuse #9" --preview
```

# mysql

| `exec` | write, default | exec "<statement>"\|@saved [params...] (tmvp write; --preview = rolled-back tx, not for DDL) |
<!-- END verbs -->

<!-- docs/llms/types/opensearch.md -->

# opensearch

OpenSearch — an alias of the [elasticsearch](elasticsearch.md) type (same fields and verbs; `ls`, `search`, `count`, `cat` … work the same).

## Fields
url (or base_url), one of api_key (`Authorization: ApiKey …`) | token (bearer) | user/password, headers, ca (`${file:secrets.ca}`), insecure; per mode. 401 → `auth_error`; 403 → `policy_blocked` (the credential lacks the privilege).

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [substring] — indices (health, docs), aliases, saved queries/*.json |
| `health` | read | health — cluster health (status, nodes, shards) |
| `indices` | read | indices [pattern] — _cat/indices (health, status, docs, size) |
| `mapping` | read | mapping <index> — one row per field: index, field (dotted), type |
| `search` | read, @item | search <index> '<json>'\|@saved [-F q=<lucene>] — hits as rows; size ≤ --limit, server timeout; @saved = queries/<name>.json (front-matter index:) |
| `count` | read | count <index> ['<json>'\|@saved] [-F q=<lucene>] |
| `cat` | read | cat <endpoint> [pattern] — allow-listed _cat endpoints: health indices aliases nodes shards allocation count segments thread_pool pending_tasks recovery templates master plugins fielddata tasks |
| `get` | read | get <index> <id> — one document |
| `index` | write, default | index <index> '<json>'\|@saved [-F id=<id>] — create/replace a document |
| `update` | write | update <index> <id> '<partial json>' — partial update (body without "doc"/"script" is wrapped in {"doc": …}) |
| `delete` | write | delete <index> <id> — delete one document |
| `update-by-query` | write | update-by-query <index> '<json with query + script>' (--preview = count; no query = every doc → needs destructive) |
| `delete-index` | destructive | delete-index <index> — no wildcards, no _all |
| `delete-by-query` | destructive | delete-by-query <index> '<json with query>' (--preview = count) |
| `reindex` | destructive | reindex '<json {"source":…,"dest":…}>' |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [substring]` = indices (non-dot), aliases and saved queries `assets/<system>/queries/<name>.json` (front-matter `index:`; `tmvp prod search @errors` runs `search`). `search` sets `size` ≤ `--limit` and a server-side `timeout`; responses are capped by `limits.bytes`.

Destructive detection: `update-by-query` without a query (or `match_all`) needs `destructive: true`; `delete-index` refuses wildcards and `_all`.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod search ls
tmvp prod search mapping logs-2026.11
tmvp all search search 'logs-*' '{"query":{"term":{"http.status":500}}}' --limit 20
tmvp prod search count orders -F q='status:failed'
tmvp prod search cat shards
tmvp write prod search index orders '{"id":1,"status":"ok"}' -F id=1 --reason "fix doc"
tmvp write prod search delete-by-query orders '{"query":{"term":{"test":true}}}' --preview --reason "drop test docs"
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/portforward.md -->

# portforward

A fixed tunnel to one remote endpoint through its own `via:` (ssh or k8s); usable as a `via:` hop.

## Fields
remote (host:port) or target (svc/x:port) + namespace for k8s, via, local_port

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — what this hop reaches: remote, via chain, local listener (no dial) |
| `status` | read | dial the remote through the tunnel; latency, listener |
| `open` | read | open a local 127.0.0.1 listener on local_port: or the tmvp port convention (= export pg-service) [-F port=N] (kept while the server keeps the system warm) |
| `close` | read | close the local listener |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = remote, via chain, listener, default local port (no dial).

## Examples
```
tmvp prod db-tunnel ls
tmvp prod db-tunnel status
tmvp prod db-tunnel open   # then: psql service=acme-prod-db (tmvp export pg-service)
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/postgres.md -->

# postgres

PostgreSQL. Reads run on `read.dsn` inside `BEGIN READ ONLY` with statement/lock timeouts and a row cap; writes on `write.dsn` in a transaction (`--preview` rolls back and reports rows affected).

## Fields
read.dsn / write.dsn (secret: `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db`), or host/port/dbname/user + password; `via:` for tunnels; `limits:`

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — saved queries (@name, all asset roots) then live tables, views, matviews |
| `health` | read | ping, server version, recovery state, latency |
| `describe` | read | describe            → tables; describe <table> → columns |
| `query` | read, @item | query "<sql>" [params...] \| query @saved [params...] (read-only tx, row cap) |
| `exec` | write, default | exec "<sql>"\|@saved [params...] (tmvp write; --preview = rolled-back tx) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = saved queries (assets `queries/*.sql`) + live tables/views/matviews; `describe <table>` = columns.

## Examples
```
tmvp all db ls
tmvp prod db describe orders
tmvp all db query "select count(*) from orders where created_at > now() - interval '1 day'" --diff
tmvp prod db @unpaid-orders 7
tmvp write prod db "update orders set status='paid' where id=42" --reason "support #812" --preview
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/prometheus.md -->

# prometheus

Prometheus HTTP API (also Thanos/Mimir/VictoriaMetrics). Read only.

## Fields
url (or base_url), token or user/password, headers, insecure

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [substring] — metric names (label __name__ values), filtered by substring, capped by --limit |
| `query` | read | query "<promql>" [-F time=RFC3339] — instant vector → one row per series |
| `range` | read | range "<promql>" [-F step=30s] — over --since (default 1h, ≤7d), one row per sample |
| `alerts` | read | alerts — active alerts (name, state, severity, since) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [substring]` = metric names.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod prom ls http_requests
tmvp all prom query "sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~\"5..\"}[5m]))"
tmvp prod prom range "up" --since 6h -F step=1m
tmvp prod prom alerts
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/redis.md -->

# redis

Redis. Only read commands on reads; SCAN is bounded (never KEYS).

## Fields
url (secret redis:// or rediss://) or read.url/write.url; optional password, tls, tls_server_name

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls [-F sep=:] — key prefixes from a bounded SCAN sample (≤5000 keys), with counts and dbsize |
| `info` | read | info [section] → key/value rows |
| `get` | read | get <key> (string values; other types → use type) |
| `scan` | read | scan [pattern] [-F type=hash] (bounded SCAN, never KEYS) |
| `ttl` | read | ttl <key> |
| `type` | read | type <key> |
| `set` | write | set <key> <value> [ttl e.g. 10m] |
| `del` | write | del <key> [key...] (literal keys, no patterns) |
| `expire` | write | expire <key> <ttl e.g. 1h> |
| `flushdb` | destructive | flushdb (destructive) |
| `flushall` | destructive | flushall (destructive) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls [-F sep=:]` = dbsize + key prefixes (count, example) from a bounded SCAN sample (≤5000 keys); values are never read.

## Examples
```
tmvp all cache ls
tmvp prod cache scan "session:*" --limit 20
tmvp prod cache ttl session:42
tmvp write prod cache del session:42 --reason "force logout"
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/script.md -->

# script

Your own scripts in `assets/<system>/scripts/` (sh, py, js, ps1, cmd, rb, shebang). `# tmvp: read` header = read; else write.

## Fields
env: {NAME: value} (values may be `${secrets.x}`; `${file:secrets.x}` → per-call path), read.env / write.env

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — saved scripts across all asset roots: name, read\|write, source file |
| `list` | read | list — alias of ls |
| `run` | read, @item | run @name [args] — only scripts declared `# tmvp: read` |
| `exec` | write, default | exec @name [args] — any script (tmvp write; --preview shows it) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` (alias `list`) = scripts across asset roots: name, read|write, source.

## Examples
```
tmvp all jobs ls
tmvp prod jobs @queue-depth
tmvp write prod jobs exec @requeue 42 --reason "stuck job" --preview
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/ssh.md -->

# ssh

SSH host and `via:` tunneler (also the `{container: name}` hop and read-only docker). Commands run under `nice`, timeout and output caps; the key is parsed in memory.

## Fields
host, port (22), user, key (`${file:secrets.x}`), passphrase, password, host_key / known_hosts (or insecure: true); read.*/write.* per mode

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | read | ls — saved scripts across all asset roots: @name, read\|write, description, source; plus running containers (name, image, status, ports) |
| `health` | read | connect, uname, uptime, latency |
| `docker` | read | docker ps [-a] \| logs <c> [--tail N] [--since X] [--timestamps] \| inspect <c> (env masked) \| stats [c] \| top <c> \| images \| compose ps \| compose logs <svc> (-F project=<dir> \| -F file=<path>) — allow-list only |
| `script` | read, @item | script @name [args...] [-F container=<c>] — saved script declared read (assets/<system>/scripts/<name>.sh); in a container via docker exec -i |
| `run` | write, default | run "<command>"\|@name [args...] [-F container=<c>] (tmvp write; nice + timeout + output caps; in a container via docker exec) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = saved scripts (`scripts/*.sh`) with read/write mode (reads need front-matter `read: true`),
plus running containers (kind `containers`: name, image, status, ports) when the ssh user can use docker.

## Docker (no docker CLI or API needed locally — everything runs over ssh)
- `docker` (read) is an allow-list; anything else, and any flag not listed, is rejected:
  `ps [-a]`, `logs <c> [--tail N] [--since X] [--timestamps]` (`--limit`/`--since` of the call fill in),
  `inspect <c>` (Config.Env values masked as `KEY=***`), `stats [c]` (always `--no-stream`), `top <c>`,
  `images`, `compose ps`, `compose logs <svc>` (with `-F project=<dir>` or `-F file=<compose.yml>`).
- Inside a container: `script @name -F container=api` (read; script must declare read) pipes the saved
  script into `docker exec -i api sh -s -- args`; `tmvp write ... "<cmd>" -F container=api --reason ...`
  runs `docker exec api sh -c '<cmd>'` (same write policy: --reason, --force on protected envs).
- Container hop: a system reaches a container's port through ssh with
  `via: [box, {container: pg}]` (or `{container: pg, network: backend}`, optional `sudo: true` → `sudo -n docker`).
  The hop must directly follow an ssh system and be last. On each new connection tmvp runs
  `docker inspect` over ssh to get the container IP (cached ≤3s; compose recreate changes it) and dials
  `<ip>:<port of the target's host:port>` from the ssh host; the target's host name is ignored.
  Errors: container not found, not running, docker not permitted (add the ssh user to the `docker` group).
- Container/service/network names must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.

## Examples
```
tmvp all bastion ls
tmvp all bastion health
tmvp prod bastion @disk
tmvp write prod bastion "systemctl restart api" --reason "deploy stuck"
tmvp prod box docker ps -a
tmvp prod box docker logs api --tail 200 --since 15m
tmvp prod box docker compose logs web -F project=/srv/app
tmvp prod box @disk -F container=api
tmvp write prod box "rm -f /tmp/cache/*" -F container=api --reason "stale cache" --force
```
Container hop config:
```yaml
box: { type: ssh, host: db.internal.example, user: deploy, key: "${file:secrets.box_key}", host_key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..." }
db:  { type: postgres, via: [box, {container: pg}], read: { dsn: "${secrets.db_ro}" } }   # dsn host ignored, port used
```

<!-- docs/llms/types/web.md -->

# web

Web apps through playwright-cli. Assets: `context.md` (login steps, never:) and `pages/*.md` (path, elements, actions, checks). click/fill/press/select/do mutate only via tmvp write.

## Fields
base_url, users: {name: {role, user, password (secret)}}, browser, login: {manual: browser}

## Verbs
<!-- BEGIN verbs (generated from the connector registry: go generate ./... ; do not edit) -->
| Verb | Mode | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `login` | read | login [-F user=ops] — run the scripted login (manual: browser → tmvp login <env> <system>) |
| `goto` | read | goto <page\|/path> — navigate (base_url + path) |
| `text` | read | text <el\|page.el> — visible text of an element |
| `snapshot` | read | snapshot [el] — accessibility snapshot (refs e1, e2 ...) |
| `screenshot` | read | screenshot [el] — PNG under ~/.tmvp/<product>/web/shots |
| `check` | read | check [page\|--all] — run the page checks |
| `ls` | read | ls — declared pages across all asset roots (path, elements, actions, source); offline |
| `pages` | read | pages — declared pages, paths, actions |
| `elements` | read | elements <page> — declared elements, locators, mutating/never |
| `click` | read-write | click <el> — read: non-mutating elements in destructive envs; else tmvp write ... click <el> --reason |
| `fill` | read-write | fill <el> <value> — as click (value never on argv) |
| `press` | read-write | press <key> — always mutating (may submit): tmvp write ... press <key> --reason |
| `select` | read-write | select <el> <value> — as click |
| `do` | read-write, default | do <action> [k=v ...] — page action; mutating ones via tmvp write (--preview resolves only) |
<!-- END verbs -->

## Discovery
`ls` = declared pages across asset roots (path, elements, actions, source) — works offline, no browser needed; `elements <page>` lists locators.

## Examples
```
tmvp prod admin ls
tmvp prod admin elements users
tmvp prod admin text users.rows
tmvp write prod admin do users.find-user email=a@b.test --reason "support #812"
```
